title: Mastering Glaucoma: From Diagnostic Workup to Pharmacotherapy
summary: An intensive guide for the ophthalmologist on the systematic diagnosis, longitudinal monitoring, and advanced pharmacological management of Glaucoma, with a specific focus on beta-blocker hemodynamics.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup: The Glaucoma Assessment
content: Step 1: Precise Goldmann Applanation Tonometry (IOP check).
Step 2: Pachymetry (Correct IOP based on central corneal thickness).
Step 3: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy (Evaluation of anterior chamber depth/Van Herick).
Step 4: Gonioscopy (Mandatory for classification of Open vs. Closed angle).
Step 5: Optic Nerve Head evaluation (Cup-to-disc ratio, neuroretinal rim thinning, NOTCHING).
Step 6: Perimetry (Humphrey Field Analyzer 24-2 or 30-2 SITA-Standard/Fast).
Step 7: Structural Imaging (OCT - RNFL thickness mapping and Ganglion Cell Complex analysis).

sections.title: Red Flags: Emergency Signs
content: Acute angle closure: IOP > 50mmHg, nausea, halos, fixed mid-dilated pupil.
Symptomatic progression: Sudden loss of central/peripheral vision.
Corneal edema obscuring view of the disc.
Inability to visualize the angle structure (gonioscopy).

sections.title: Beta-Blockers: Mechanism & Contraindications
content: Mechanism: Blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors in the ciliary body epithelium; reduces aqueous humor production by decreasing cAMP levels.
Absolute Contraindications: Asthma, COPD, symptomatic bradycardia, second/third-degree heart block, overt heart failure.
Clinical Pearl: Non-selective (Timolol) has higher risk of systemic respiratory side effects compared to Beta-1 selective (Betaxolol).
